haiku-low.q1: It still signs in. The account is found by the unchanged Google sub, and the new email changes nothing, since only sub is stored and users.email is never rewritten.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the matched account's correct password on the confirmation form within the 10-minute window. A correct password links the Google account and starts a session.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account locks for 15 minutes and the pending link is deleted. Before that, the form is re-shown with the generic message and the pending record keeps its original TTL.
haiku-low.q4: Verified email matching no user: a user is created with no password and email_verified_at set, linked to the Google sub, and signed in. Email not verified: refused, nothing created, user sent to login page to use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: NOT STATED for the exact wording of the error page. Both cases fail: the attempt expired or was already consumed by GETDEL, so the error page shows and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row with a sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax), same as password login. The sessions row named by any existing sid cookie the browser sent is deleted first.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. If the sub is linked to any user, or the user already has a Google link, it is refused and nothing changes. Otherwise the link is inserted with no new session.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under goog:attempt:STATE, which holds nonce, PKCE verifier, bind value, origin, next and user_id. GETDEL removes it at the first callback whatever the outcome; otherwise its 600 s TTL expires it.
haiku-low.q9: Held in Redis as goog:pending:ID holding sub, target user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the g_pending cookie plus an HMAC confirm token in the form. Deleted on success, lockout, double submit, or TTL expiry.
haiku-low.q10: In PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts, with user_id as primary key and sub unique. Those database constraints enforce one link per user and one user per Google account; the code's pre-check is only for friendly messages.
haiku-low.q11: The origin page (login or Settings) shows Could not complete Google sign-in, try again; the reason is logged and nothing is written. It is not retried: the attempt is already consumed, so the user restarts.
haiku-low.q12: By the attempt's origin field, login or settings. A settings attempt stores the starting user_id; the callback requires the g_bind cookie to match and the signed-in session user to equal that stored user_id.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes for them. Accounts are identified by sub, never email, and a linked sub signs in even if the email changed or email_verified is false. They get start_session.
sonnet.q2: They must prove ownership by password. A pending link is created (Redis goog:pending:ID, 600s), g_pending cookie set, and a password form shown. POST /auth/google/confirm needs the confirm token, the g_pending cookie and the Redis record. The password is checked with check_password_with_lockout and the account must not be locked. Only on a correct password is the link inserted and start_session called.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 failures locked_until is set to now plus 15 minutes and failed_logins resets to 0. Then the pending record is deleted, g_pending is cleared, and 'Account temporarily locked' is shown. The half-finished link is discarded and no link or session is made. Before lockout, the form is re-shown with a generic wrong-password message and the pending record and its original TTL stay.
sonnet.q4: If the verified email matches no user, one DB transaction creates a user (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) and the user_google_accounts row, then signs them in with start_session. If email_verified is false, it refuses, points to email and password, and creates nothing.
sonnet.q5: Error page, nothing changes. After 12 minutes the attempt record has expired (TTL 600s). A second load of the same callback URL finds the record already deleted by GETDEL. An unknown, expired or used state is rejected.
sonnet.q6: No new session type. It is the same start_session(user_id) as a password login. It deletes the sessions row named by the sid cookie the browser sent, if any, inserts a new sessions row and sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). It then redirects to the stored next or /home.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match is required, and email_verified is not required. If the sub is already linked to any user, it goes back to Settings with 'already linked to a user' and nothing changes. The same happens if this user already has a Google link. A race unique violation is handled the same way. The session stays as is.
sonnet.q8: They are in the Redis attempt record goog:attempt:STATE (with the bind value, origin, next and user_id for settings). The state is sent to Google. The record is deleted atomically by GETDEL at the first callback whatever the outcome. Otherwise it expires after the 600s TTL.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis as goog:pending:ID, containing sub, target user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the g_pending cookie, which holds the ID, and by the confirm token (an HMAC of the ID) in the form. It is deleted on success (GETDEL), on lockout, or on a double submit. Otherwise it expires after the 600s TTL from the callback.
sonnet.q10: In the PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts (user_id, sub, linked_at). user_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so a user has at most one Google account. sub is UNIQUE, so a Google account links to at most one user. The database constraints enforce both rules.
sonnet.q11: The user is sent back to the origin page (login or Settings) with the message 'Could not complete Google sign-in, try again'. The specific reason is logged but not shown, and nothing is written. The exchange is not retried, because the attempt is already consumed. The user must restart.
sonnet.q12: The attempt record stores an origin (login or settings), and the callback branches on it. For a settings attempt, the record holds the starting user's user_id. At the callback the signed-in session user must equal that user_id, otherwise it gives the error page. The link is then attached to that user.
